title: How to Build a Weekly Study Plan
strategy_problem: Without a structured plan, students often study passively (just watching YouTube videos) or focus entirely on their strongest skill because it's comfortable, neglecting their weaknesses. 'Studying IELTS' for 4 hours vaguely is less effective than 1 hour of targeted, strategic practice.
core_framework: 1. The 80/20 Weakness Rule: Dedicate 80% of your study time to your weakest skill (e.g., Writing) and 20% to maintaining your strong skills. Stop practicing what you are already good at.

2. Daily Active Input: Every day, engage in 30 minutes of 'active input'—listening to a podcast or reading an article *while* noting down collocations and new sentence structures. This is not test practice; it's language building.

3. Segmented Practice vs. Full Mocks: Don't do full mock tests every day. Do 'segmented practice' (e.g., just Writing Task 1 intro paragraphs, or just Listening Part 3). Reserve full 3-hour mock tests for the weekend to build stamina.
4. The Review Block: For every hour of practice, schedule at least 30 minutes of review. A study plan without a dedicated review block is useless.
ielts_scenario: A student needs a 7.0 overall, with a minimum of 6.5 in all bands. They are scoring 8.0 in Reading, 7.5 in Listening, but 5.5 in Writing. Despite this, they spend 2 hours a day doing Reading and Listening tests because it makes them feel successful. They fail the exam because their Writing remains at 5.5.

do: Schedule specific tasks (e.g., 'Tuesday 7pm: Write two Task 1 overviews', not just 'Tuesday: Study Writing').
Force yourself to study your weakest skill first thing in your study session.
Take one full, timed mock test every weekend to build physical stamina for the real exam.
dont: Count passive watching of IELTS YouTube videos as 'study time'.
Practice your strongest skill more than your weakest skill.
Skip the review phase just to do more practice tests.

example_application: A targeted Wednesday plan: 6:00 PM - Active reading of a BBC article (noting 5 new collocations). 6:30 PM - Segmented practice: Write only the introductions for three different Task 2 prompts. 7:15 PM - Review: Check grammar using AI/tutor feedback.
personal_action_step: Create a schedule for the next 7 days. Identify your weakest skill. Block out 4 specific 45-minute sessions dedicated *only* to that skill, focusing on a different micro-task each time (e.g., intro writing, idea generation, grammar review).
image_prompt_fallback: A physical weekly planner open on a desk. The word 'WRITING' is blocked out multiple times in red marker, highlighting a focus on weaknesses.

quiz.question: What is the most effective way to allocate study time when preparing for the IELTS?

options.A: Divide time equally (25%) among Reading, Writing, Listening, and Speaking.
options.B: Spend the majority of your time doing full 3-hour practice tests every day.
options.C: Dedicate the vast majority of your study time to your weakest skill, while doing minimal maintenance on your strong skills.

quiz.explanation: Because IELTS often requires minimum scores in *each* band, your overall success is gated by your weakest skill. Practicing what you are already good at provides diminishing returns.
